summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed an award of a stepdaughter's custody to her stepfather and directed that custody be placed with her mother, holding that a court may not award custody to a third party under a best-interests test without first finding exceptional circumstances, which in every case upheld by the court had meant a psychological-parent relationship formed during the third party's actual physical custody.
key_cases.relevance: Instructs that where a parent's fitness to provide minimally adequate care is genuinely at issue, the route is a ch. 27-20 deprivation proceeding commenced for that purpose, not a fitness ruling inside a divorce custody case.
key_cases.quote: Absent exceptional circumstances the natural parent is entitled to custody of the child even though the third party may be able to offer more amenities.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an adjudication that a ten-year-old was deprived by reason of parental alienation and psychological maltreatment, holding the finding of deprivation by clear and convincing evidence was not clearly erroneous and that the juvenile court had not improperly merged the divorce-related custody dispute with the deprivation proceeding.
key_cases.relevance: Addresses the case that enters the child-welfare system out of ongoing civil litigation: the district court deferred its visitation ruling to the deprivation proceeding, and the court held that ch. 27-20 hearings must be conducted separately from proceedings outside juvenile-court jurisdiction even though judicial notice of prior adjudications is permitted.
key_cases.quote: A juvenile court's finding of deprivation must be supported by clear and convincing evidence.

state_agency.name: North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services
state_agency.hotline: 1-833-958-3500 (8 a.m.-5 p.m. Central / 7 a.m.-4 p.m. Mountain, Mon-Fri; if a child is in immediate danger call 911)

mandatory_reporters: Listed professionals only — North Dakota is not a universal-reporting state (N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(1))
Tier 1, 2, 3, and 4 mental health professionals (as defined in N.D. Cent. Code § 25-01-01) and any other medical or mental health professional
Religious practitioners of the healing arts
Schoolteachers, school administrators, and school counselors
Child care workers and child care licensors
Juvenile court personnel and probation officers
Licensed social workers and family service specialists
Members of the clergy, except when the knowledge is derived from information received as a spiritual adviser
Any person who discovers images of sexual conduct by a child on a workplace computer (N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(3))
reporting_details: North Dakota is not a universal-reporting state: the professionals listed in N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(1) must immediately report orally or in writing to the Department of Health and Human Services or its authorized agent, while any other person may report (N.D. Cent. Code §§ 50-25.1-03(2), 50-25.1-04(1)).

other: A child placed for care or adoption in violation of law

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately if there is a serious threat to the child's life or health; otherwise within department-set time frames

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: An extension of time must be requested of and granted by the department (N.D. Admin. Code § 75-03-19-04).
